Transaction health

A decision-focused view of transaction outcomes, fees and fraud flags

Jan–May 2026 · GBP

Executive Summary

  • Completion is very low. Only about 2.6% of attempted value (£48,933.55 of £1,897,267.75) completes; 60% of transactions fail.
  • Flags are customer-level. All 300 fraud flags come from 4 customers; every transaction for those customers is flagged, while the other 16 have 0%. Rajan Mehta alone accounts for 59% of attempted value (£1,124,545.45), has £0 completed value, and all 75 of his transactions are Reversed. Merchant-category flag differences are not reliable.
  • Fees need a rule review. All £750.17 is on non-Completed transactions, including £262.53 on Pending. International transfers are £399.61 below the £2.50 standard across 200 rows; international ATM fees are mixed: 25 rows above £1.50 and 75 at £0.
  • Merchant risk labels do not separate risk. Fraud-flag rates are 19.88% for High, 22.30% for Medium and 18.97% for Low, against 20.00% overall.
Finance + Product · 30 daysReview fee rules across all international-transfer and international-ATM rows; reconcile the £399.61 transfer gap and resolve the 25 above-standard ATM charges.
Risk · 10 business daysReview the customer-level flagging logic and complete a documented review of all 4 flagged customers and all 300 flags.
Product + Data · 30 daysCapture a failed_reason for 100% of failed transactions; only 300 of 900 currently have one.

Data limitations

Only 20 customers are represented. The data covers January–May 2026 only; the H2 run-rate is illustrative, not a forecast. Segment, region and KYC comparisons are indicative because customer attributes are not independently distributed. Fraud flags appear customer-level, so merchant-category differences should not be treated as reliable risk signals.

Source: v_txn_master · 1 row per transaction
